Application Materials.content:
LSE carefully considers each application and takes into account all the information included on your application form, such as your:
- academic achievement (including predicted and achieved grades)
- statement of academic purpose
- two academic references
- CV
- GRE/GMAT
[See further information on supporting documents](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/Prospective-students/Supporting-documents). All applicants without a UK undergraduate degree must submit GMAT or GRE test scores with their application.

Application Deadlines.content:
Academic year 2026/27 start date: **Early September 2026**.
Application deadline: **None – rolling admissions**. Applications for this programme are considered on a rolling basis and will close once the programme is full; there is no fixed deadline.
To be considered for funding opportunities, you must submit your application and all supporting documents by the funding deadline. The funding deadline for needs-based awards from LSE is **23 April 2026**.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **Upper second-class honours degree (2:1) or equivalent** in **any discipline** and **good quantitative skills, at least to A-level Mathematics (or the equivalent)**.
- For applicants from China, to be considered for admission to a taught master's programme (**upper second class equivalent**), LSE would normally require **a bachelor's degree with an overall mark of 85 per cent** from applicants who have attended a highly regarded institution in China, while all other applicants are normally required to obtain **a mark of at least 90 per cent**.

GRE GMAT Requirements.content:
All applicants without a UK undergraduate degree must submit GMAT or GRE test scores with their application. Applicants with UK undergraduate degrees, particularly those whose quantitative skills are not demonstrated by their undergraduate studies, may be asked to submit GMAT or GRE scores. [Find out more about GRE/GMAT](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/Prospective-students/Entry-requirements/GRE-and-GMAT)
Applications are carefully considered taking into account information included on the application form, including CV and GRE/GMAT. Check if you're [exempt from taking the GRE/GMAT](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/Prospective-students/Entry-requirements/GRE-and-GMAT).

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
The English language requirement for this programme is **Standard**. [Read more about LSE English language requirements](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/Prospective-students/Entry-requirements/English-language-requirements).
- English tests must be **less than two years old by 1 October** of your start year.
- These are **minimum** requirements; selectors may require a higher score at their discretion.
- Additional language instruction (Presessional/Insessional) may be needed before registration.
- **IELTS** must be IELTS *Academic* (not General); online version accepted.
- **PTEA** is accepted **in-person only** (online not accepted).
- **Cambridge**: for older tests, an online converter is used; C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency preferred.

Program Overview.content:
MSc Accounting and Data Analytics is a Graduate (Taught) programme in the Department of Accounting. Study mode / programme availability is full-time for Home and Overseas students, with a duration of 10 months. The academic year is 2026/27, the start date is Early September 2026, and the location is Houghton Street, London.
The MSc Accounting and Data Analytics is designed for students who want to understand how roles in accounting, investment banking, and asset management are being reshaped by advances in data science, technology, and digital transformation. Throughout the programme, students develop both theoretical foundations and applied skills across accounting, financial management, data analytics, and computer programming, preparing them for roles that demand a strong understanding of business fundamentals alongside the ability to analyse, model, and interpret complex data.
A defining feature of the programme is its integration of accounting fundamentals with applied data science. Developed in response to growing demand within the investment industry, the programme emphasises the use of analytical tools in key areas such as financial reporting, forecasting, corporate valuation, and performance analysis. It is designed to equip students with financial insight and technical capability valued by data-driven financial and non-financial institutions.
Graduates will be prepared for roles in asset management, private equity, investment banking, corporate finance, ESG analytics, and management consulting. The programme also appeals to students seeking to work in audit and assurance functions that increasingly rely on data-driven approaches. Students benefit from LSE’s location in London, with opportunities to connect with leading financial institutions through employer events, alumni panels, and industry-focused public lectures, complemented by tailored career support throughout the year.
The programme begins with a pre-sessional programme in early September, including preparatory classes in quantitative methods, financial accounting, and management accounting, along with professional development sessions, career, networking, and social events designed to help students connect with faculty and fellow students. Its primary aim is to ensure that all students, regardless of academic background, reach a shared level of knowledge and understanding.
In the first term, students take courses designed to develop advanced skills in both accounting and data analytics. The foundational accounting courses build understanding of how economic activity is captured and communicated through financial statements, while data analytics training combines applied regression, computer programming, and data management and visualisation. In the second term, students take two bespoke core courses exclusive to the degree programme: Advanced Financial Statement Analysis and Forensic Accounting Analytics. The programme also includes electives in both accounting and data analytics, allowing students to tailor the degree to areas such as M&A analysis, ESG disclosure evaluation, management control, machine learning, or natural language processing.
Following the pre-sessional programme, students take examined courses totalling four full units over the academic year. On average, students can expect around 12 hours of contact time per week, including lectures and seminars, alongside independent study. Teaching is informed by the research of LSE faculty active in academic and policy debates in accounting, finance, and data science. Courses are delivered through lectures, classes, and seminars, and faculty use teaching methods including case discussions, programming tasks, group projects, and data-driven problem sets.
Assessment is based on a combination of formal summative evaluations and formative assessments. Summative assessments typically include written examinations, essays, and project work, while formative assessments such as problem sets, class exercises, or group presentations provide feedback without affecting final marks.
Graduates of the MSc in Accounting and Data Analytics will be well equipped for careers at the intersection of finance, accounting, and data science. Typical roles include financial analyst, asset manager, investment banking associate, private equity analyst, forensic accountant, ESG analyst, and management consultant, particularly in firms that prioritise data-driven decision-making. Potential employers span investment banks, hedge funds, consulting firms, asset managers, and audit and advisory firms. The programme also provides a foundation for roles in audit, assurance, financial advisory, ESG strategy, risk analytics, compliance, technology and fintech strategy or product teams, and data science roles requiring domain-specific expertise in finance and accounting. It also serves as preparation for research-focused degrees, including PhD programmes in accounting, finance, or data science.
Top 5 sectors Department of Accounting students work in:
- Financial and Professional Services
- Accounting and Auditing
- FMCG, Manufacturing and Retail
- Consultancy
- Education, Teaching and Research
The Department of Accounting at LSE is recognised worldwide for the excellence of its research and teaching, ranked eighth in the world in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026. The department has a long-standing research tradition and has explored the role of accounting in firms, markets, and the economy. It was ranked the top place in the UK to study accounting by the Guardian University Guide in its 2025 and 2026 league tables. Each year, the department admits around 375 students across undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.

You'll attend a pre-sessional programme in early September. The pre-sessional programme includes preparatory classes in quantitative methods, financial accounting, and management accounting, along with professional development sessions, career, networking, and social events designed to help students connect with faculty and fellow students. The primary aim of the pre-sessional programme is to ensure that all students — regardless of their academic background — reach a shared level of knowledge and understanding.
Following this, you take examined courses totalling **four full units** over the academic year. On average, you can expect around **12 hours of contact time per week**, including lectures and seminars. Courses are delivered through a combination of lectures, classes, and seminars.

Cost of Attendance.content:
[LSE broadly estimates that students should allow £1,550 per month](https://info.lse.ac.uk/current-students/immigration-advice/applying-for-a-Student-visa) for all living expenses, including accommodation, travel, food, laundry, study costs, and other personal expenses.
- Private housing costs can vary considerably depending on location and accommodation type, but start at approximately **£650 per month**.
- Food costs will account for a significant part of your budget. LSE estimates that students will spend **£150-£300 per month** on food, depending on whether they live in catered or self-catered halls, or whether they live in private accommodation.

Financial Aid.content:
Applications are considered on a rolling basis, but if you’d like to be considered for any funding opportunities, you must submit your application and all supporting documents by the funding deadline.
- **Fee reduction:** Students who have completed and passed an undergraduate degree at LSE and are beginning taught graduate study at the School are eligible for a **10 per cent tuition fee reduction**. Students who have completed and passed two or more Summer School courses are eligible for a **five per cent reduction**. If you meet the eligibility criteria for both discounts, the higher **10 per cent** discount rate will apply. [Find out more about the LSE alumni discount](https://info.lse.ac.uk/staff/divisions/Finance-Division/Fees-Income-and-Credit-Control/Rewards-and-Discounts).
- **Scholarships and other funding:** LSE provides scholarships to help both home and overseas students. It offers some needs-based awards for this programme, including the [Graduate Support Scheme](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding/secure/graduate-support-scheme) and the [LSE Excellence Scholarship](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding/LSE-Excellence-Scholarship). Competition for these awards and scholarships is strong.
- To apply for an award, you must have an offer of a place and submit a Graduate Financial Support application before the funding deadline. The funding deadline for needs-based awards from LSE is **23 April 2026**.
- In addition to needs-based awards, LSE offers [scholarships for students from specific regions of the world](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding) and [awards for certain subjects](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding/Department-or-programme-specific-funding).
- You can’t apply for a Graduate Support Scheme or LSE scholarship once you’ve joined the School. LSE expects students who register for a programme to have sufficient funds for the duration.
- At LSE, your tuition fees, and eligibility for any financial support, will depend on whether you’re classified as a home or overseas student.

Multiple Applications.content:
You may submit an application via the online application system only **ONCE** within the application cycle (**October 2025 to September 2026**).
When completing your initial online application, you may choose up to **two programmes** in order of preference. **If you are applying for two programmes, please submit a separate statement of academic purpose for each programme**. Your choices will be considered in sequence, and it is only possible to hold one offer of a place, so if you are offered a place on your first-choice programme you will not be considered for your second-choice unless you specifically request it.
If you are unsuccessful in your application to both of your initially chosen programmes and you wish to be considered for further, additional choices, you may do this by submitting the **Add/Amend programmes** form via the [Graduate Applicant Portal](https://lseportal.force.com/admissions/s/track-my-graduate-application) and paying an additional administrative fee of **£105**. You should not use this form to add choices 3 and 4 before receiving a decision on each of your original programme choices, unless you wish to withdraw your initial programme choices.
**You may only submit an application using the online application system ONCE in the same admissions cycle. If you submit a second online application within the same admissions cycle, it will not be considered.** **To apply to further programmes after you have submitted your initial online application, you must use the process above.**

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
LSE has a no-deferrals policy for offers for graduate programmes. The only exception to this is in cases of unforeseen illness or bereavement.
If a deferral is agreed in exceptional circumstances, you must submit a deferral deposit as requested in your deferral letter, using the student self-funding [payment portal](https://portal.lse.ac.uk/payments/s/fees). The deposit must be received by the **January 31st deadline** to secure your new offer for next year. The deferral deposit is offset against your tuition fees once you register.
If your circumstances match the exceptional circumstances, you may request to defer your offer using the Extenuating Circumstances form on the Graduate Applicant Portal. If your request is agreed, your offer for the current year will be declined automatically, as you do not intend to come to LSE in this cycle.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
Any offer of admission will be subject to proof of your English language score. If you have not taken a test by the time you apply, your application can still be considered without it, but **any offer will be conditional on the required score**.
- If you are set an English language condition, you may be able to take an [English Pre-sessional course at the LSE Language Centre](https://www.lse.ac.uk/language-centre/english-programmes/english-presessional-programme).
- **If you are set an English language condition, we encourage you to book a test at your earliest opportunity**.
- English tests must be **less than two years old on 1 October 2026**.
- If you are unable to take one of LSE’s preferred tests, it may be possible to take an alternative test such as Duolingo or IELTS Indicator and supplement your score by taking the LSE Language Centre Assessment; to request this option, complete the extenuating circumstances form on the GAP, providing any existing test scores and reasons why you are unable to take one of the listed tests.
- On rare occasions, LSE may accept scores below its minimum requirements if there are extenuating circumstances surrounding test scores, but **under NO CIRCUMSTANCES** will it accept scores that do not meet UKVI’s English proficiency requirements for a student visa, because the applicant would not be granted entry to the UK with such a score and LSE will therefore not issue a CAS.
